prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single objectively “best” roofing company for all Dallas roof replacements — the right contractor depends on your location, roof type, budget, timing, insurance needs and whether you want the highest-end warranty or best value. I can help you find a short list, but first here are practical, reliable steps and criteria to identify the best contractor for your job.

What to look for (must-haves)
- Proper insurance: general liability + workers’ comp (verify certificates).
- Local experience and physical address in the Dallas area (not a storm-chaser).
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT, Owens Corning Preferred, etc.) — these matter for extended warranties.
- Written, itemized estimate (labor, materials, disposal, permits, removal vs. overlay).
- Permits and code compliance: contractor should pull permits and handle inspections.
- Clear warranty: manufacturer warranty + contractor workmanship warranty (get both in writing and understand transferability).
- Good reviews and verifiable references (recent jobs in your neighborhood, photos).
- BBB rating or complaint history and search of court/claim records if you’re doing an insurance job.
- No large up-front cash payments; typical structure is modest deposit, progress payments, final payment after completion and cleanup.

Red flags
- Door-to-door “storm” salespeople pressuring you to sign immediately.
- Only cash payments, or contractor asks you to sign incomplete paperwork.
- Vague scope or no tear-off details, no permit plan, or refuses to back warranty in writing.
- Significantly lower price than all other bids without explanation.

Key questions to ask every contractor
- How long have you been serving Dallas? Can you provide 3 local references and photos of recent jobs?
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide insurance certificates and contractor registration?
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle/roof system you propose? What warranties are offered?
- Will you pull permits? Who does inspections?
- What is included in your price (ice/water shield, ridge vents, drip edge, flashing, tear-off disposal)?
- Timeline for start and completion, and payment schedule?
- How do you handle unforeseen problems (rot, decking replacement, change orders)?
- Will you provide lien waivers and a final sign-off checklist?

How to pick among bids
- Compare apples-to-apples: same materials, ventilation, underlayment, number of tear-offs, flashing details.
- Prefer the contractor that explains ventilation, attic issues, and long-term care (not just lowest price).
- Check manufacturer certification — those contractors will often handle warranty claims for you.

If you’re filing an insurance claim
- Make sure the contractor explains the claim process and how payments are handled; beware of contractors who want your insurance checks outright.
- Get the scope in writing and note if they will act as your public adjuster (must be licensed).

Next steps I can help with
- If you want, tell me your Dallas ZIP code and whether this is residential or commercial, roof material preference, and if you’re working with insurance. I’ll give a tailored checklist and a sample message/email you can send to contractors to request estimates and compare bids.
- I can also draft a short list of interview questions and a scoring template to help choose the best local contractor.

Would you like me to: (A) help draft an email to send to contractors, or (B) give the interview checklist and scoring template, or (C) get started by telling me your ZIP code and roof details so I can tailor recommendations?
